subject: Clarifying security add-on invoicing and pilot credit options for NorthStar
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@northstarhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@northstarhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifying security addon invoicing for pilot and production

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the flow and observability looked good. Before we lock internal approval, procurement asked us to confirm a couple of commercial items around the compliance/security add-ons (audit logs, KMS/HSM, residency):

- Can you outline options for handling the one-time implementation/evidence delivery work vs. recurring charges? Procurement prefers to avoid large up-front capital line items.
- For HSM: we need clarity on seat-based vs throughput-based billing and whether seats can be amortized across the first 6–12 months as a credit.
- Residency: if we start in hosted but plan an on-prem migration later in the year, how do you propose credits/true-ups work?

Also, could you attach any sample amortization schedules or a concise worksheet showing unit economics across low/medium/high usage? That will speed the internal finance review.

We’d like to keep the pilot under a single PO if possible.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Director, Platform Engineering
NorthStar Health
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@northstarhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying security addon invoicing for pilot and production

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (revenue) and Tessa (offerings) so we can provide a short set of practical pathways. At a high level we typically present three options (we can attach a worksheet):

1) One-time implementation + recurring addon: Classic model. Implementation is charged up front; audit-evidence delivery and HSM provisioning are billed as one-time professional fees. Audit logs / KMS are then recurring.

2) Amortized implementation credit: We invoice implementation to a contract line item but provide a monthly credit against recurring usage for X months (6 or 12). This keeps PO/outflow spread.

3) Bundled pilot package: Small fixed monthly pilot fee that includes a capped set of audit events, temporary HSM seat access, and one evidence delivery run. If you convert to production we reconcile and either invoice the remaining seat cost or continue amortization per agreed schedule.

Notes on HSM seats vs throughput: seats are easiest for audit scoping and SLA alignment (dedicated HSM instances); throughput billing (per-call) scales better if you have highly variable token volumes. We can model both — I’ll attach a short worksheet that shows the blended monthly cost under each.

Residency transition: common pattern is a credit reserve line where we hold back a portion of the implementation fee for reconciliation at migration. If migration occurs within the agreed window (e.g., 9 months), we absorb transition engineering and apply credits on the remaining balance.

Attaching a compact "security-econ-grid.xlsx" that shows sample amortization (6/12 months), seat vs throughput breakout, and an example PO-friendly invoice schedule.

Would you like us to propose a specific option and numbers for the pilot (12-node seat example + audit log retention 90 days)? We can then produce a short PO-ready proposal.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, GTM Security & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

(attachment: security-econ-grid.xlsx)
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@northstarhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@northstarhealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-31T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying security addon invoicing for pilot and production

Olga — this is helpful, thanks. Quick clarifications from procurement and finance:

- Our preference is option 2 (amortized implementation). Can you show a 12-month amortization (monthly credit) and also a 6-month alternative for comparison?
- For HSM we are leaning seat-based for the pilot. For graphing to finance please show: seat cost, monthly credit, and effective monthly delta to our bill.
- Residency: we will almost certainly request on-prem in Q4. Please include a migration true-up example assuming migration in month 9.
- SOC2 / evidence: procurement wants the SOC2 attestations and a sample delivery timeline for evidence — we’ll need that attached or linked.

Finally — is there a way to keep initial pilot under the same PO as our current sandbox spend (we already have a PO open through May 2028)? If so, we’d prefer that to reduce overhead.

If you can send a PO-ready proposal with the 6/12 amortization rows and HSM-seat pricing we will fast-track internal approvals.

Cheers,
Alex
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@northstarhealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying security addon invoicing for pilot and production

Alex / Olga — attaching a PO-friendly proposal (northstar-proposal-v2.pdf) with two amortization paths and a pilot bundle. Summary here to speed things up:

- Option A (6-month amortization): Upfront implementation fee $36,000; credited back $6,000/mo for 6 months. HSM seat (pilot x12 seats) $2,500/seat/month, no additional throughput charge for pilot cap 500k calls/month.
- Option B (12-month amortization): Upfront implementation fee $36,000; credited back $3,000/mo for 12 months. HSM seat same as above.
- Pilot bundle: $8,000/month that includes 4 seats, 90-day audit log retention, and one evidence delivery run. If you scale past the pilot caps we convert to seat+recurring pricing with the remaining credit applied.

Residency migration: we propose a migration reserve equal to 25% of the implementation fee held for reconciliation; if migration happens within 9 months Redwood covers migration labor up to $12k and applies reserve toward any additional infra delta.

SOC2 evidence: certificate and sample evidence set included in the proposal PDF (section 2).

We can bill pilot under your existing PO — finance is fine as long as the PO's scope covers the billing codes in the attachment. Ben — can you confirm the PO code mapping?

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

(attachment: northstar-proposal-v2.pdf)

3) We’ll bill to your existing PO number (please reply with PO #) and attach SOC2 artifacts.
